name: Lua
summary: A lightweight embeddable language implemented as a C library with register-based bytecode interpretation, coroutine states, extensible metatables, and automatic incremental or generational garbage collection.

features.name: Embeddable C-library runtime
features.description: Lua is implemented as a C library, and the standalone lua program is a host that invokes the library. The C API represents a lua_State with call frames, a value stack, and runtime state used by the interpreter and coroutines.
benefits: Allows hosts to execute chunks and register C functions
Keeps the language core small and reusable across host applications
costs: The host must manage state and protected error boundaries
C integration exposes lifetime and calling-convention responsibilities

features.name: Register-based bytecode interpreter
features.description: Lua compiles chunks into instructions for a virtual machine and executes them through a register-based interpreter loop. The fixed lvm.c source implements luaV_execute over a CallInfo frame and instruction stream.
benefits: Provides a compact execution representation for interpreted chunks
Makes call frames and register values explicit runtime state
costs: Interpretation adds dispatch overhead compared with native execution
Frame, stack, and instruction invariants must be maintained

features.name: Resumable coroutines with automatic memory management
features.description: Lua coroutines suspend only at explicit yield points and resume from the saved execution state. Lua automatically manages runtime objects with incremental or generational collection; the fixed source maintains collector state and object lists.
benefits: Supports cooperative suspension without requiring OS threads
Provides automatic reclamation with selectable collection strategies
costs: Cooperative scheduling requires explicit yield points
Collection timing and tuning affect performance and resource behavior

features.name: Metatable-driven semantic extension boundary
features.description: Lua uses metatables to customize operations such as indexing, arithmetic, calls, and finalization. Full userdata is created and modified through the C API, providing a host-controlled data boundary.
benefits: Allows host and language values to expose domain-specific behavior
Keeps userdata storage under C-side control while enabling Lua-level operations
costs: Operator behavior can be dynamically redirected
Finalizers and host-owned data require careful lifetime coordination

mathematical_views.question: How do a host call, bytecode frame, register state, coroutine yield, and resume compose into Lua execution?
assumptions: lua_State and CallInfo frames are modeled as explicit execution state
Bytecode dispatch is a transition over register values and the current frame
The model abstracts C ABI details and instruction-level performance

mathematical_views.question: How do Lua object reachability, collector modes, weak structures, and finalizers affect object lifetime?
assumptions: Managed objects form a graph rooted in live Lua and host-visible state
Incremental and generational modes are alternative collector transition strategies
The view does not model every allocator or platform-specific tuning behavior

costs: Host code owns state and error-boundary responsibilities
Yield points and collector tuning constrain behavior

benefits: Extensible semantics and controlled userdata bridge
costs: Dynamic dispatch and finalization complicate reasoning
